messages:
Rae (PM): Kicking off a narrower spec for private deploy upgrades. Problem: field customers hit unpredictable host-network changes during operator upgrades. We need installer presets + deterministic handshake checks before any change that touches host networking.

Ethan (infra): Proposal: introduce installer presets: minimal, standard, network-managed. Minimal = no host changes, operator sidecars only. Standard = opt-in host routing edits. Network-managed = full peering/NAT changes (requires netops sign-off). CLI flag: --preset=minimal|standard|network-managed

Lina (field): Field asks: a) ability to run a "preflight" that simulates changes without applying them, b) signed bundle we can give to customer to run offline (airgap), c) clear rollback steps.

Vik (neteng): For preflight we can run a read-only job that collects routing table + firewall tests + egress mapping. Output should include: egress-ip candidates, required firewall ports, BGP neighbor status. Example: 
```
preflight: PASS
egress_candidates: [10.0.0.45]
firewall: 443/tcp OK, 179/tcp WARN
bgp: established -> next-hop 192.0.2.1
```
Store result in assets bucket with checksum so field can audit.

Rae (PM): Launch gates idea: 1) preflight PASS on pilot customers (3 topologies), 2) signed-bundle verification for airgap customers, 3) canary cohort of 5 installs with 30m observation window, 4) auto-rollback on >2% critical failures. Thoughts?

Ethan (infra): Agree. Add instrumentation: handshake_span_id on upgrades; surface in console. Also add installer "dry-run" mode that prints planned host edits and a sha256 of the signed bundle. CLI: 
```
installer install --preset=network-managed --dry-run | jq .plan
plan.sha256: abcd1234...
```

Lina (field): Can we make approval flow UI-friendly? For network-managed installs require: checkbox "Netops approval received" + upload of signed-bundle checksum. And create an audit event for compliance.

Vik (neteng): We need explicit firewall docs per preset and a mapping for common firewall solutions (Fortinet, Palo Alto, AWS SG). Also require option --preserve-egress-ip=true to attempt sticky NAT; default false. If preserve fails, preflight must WARN and list mitigations.

ops-bot: ops-bot: nightly preflight-run scheduled for pilot-customer-7 at 03:00 UTC

Rae (PM): Action list: 
- Ethan: spec installer presets + dry-run output (ETA 5d)
- Vik: firewall mapping + egress-preserve behavior doc (ETA 4d)
- Lina: signed-bundle workflow and airgap checklist (ETA 3d)
I'll draft launch criteria page and coordinate pilot list.

Ethan (infra): One more: for upgrades that must change iptables/host routes we should gate on operator immutability level. If operator image digest changes but syscall surface doesn't, allow automatic. If syscall changes, require manual approval. We'll add a simple comparison of image change types to the upgrade plan.

Lina (field): Agree. Please make rollback quick: documented playbook + a CLI "installer revert --to-image=<sha>" that performs deterministic revert and replays preflight in verify mode.

Vik (neteng): I'll add a checklist for netops sign-off capturing: peering ASNs, egress test endpoints, and expected BGP attributes. Also recommend keeping a small "fallback relay" (our managed relay that preserves customer egress) for the first two cohorts.

Rae (PM): Great. We'll iterate on the WIP spec in /docs/private/upgrade-presets.md. Quick ask: keep presets conservative and explicit. If anyone has a customer to nominate for pilot, DM me.
